To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stacking of two Fresnel zone plates is a promising approach for the fabrication of high resolution X-ray lenses.
the angular spectrum method is an efficient tool for the simulation of X-ray optics.

the X-ray focusing performance of the stacked zone plate is significantly better than that of the single zone plate, especially at low energy, and that the performance is not limited by the aberration introduced by the stacking process, but is limited by the aberrations introduced by the individual zone plates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the simulation of X-ray imaging and focusing systems.
the simulation of X-ray optics and the design of X-ray focusing optics for future synchrotron radiation sources.
the design and fabrication of Fresnel zone plates for X-ray focusing, and the evaluation of the focusing properties of these lenses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of two zone plates is not an efficient way to achieve high-resolution imaging.
stacking of two Fresnel zone plates is a viable and attractive approach for high-resolution focusing of X-rays.
the use of the two zone plates in a stack configuration would be a very good solution to the problem of high-resolution focusing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stacking of two zone plates with different zone widths is not a good approach for the X-ray microscopy.
the optimized stacking of two high resolution zone plates is a promising way for X-ray microscopy.
the optimized stacked zone plate can be used to improve the resolution of a zone plate with an efficiency of about 80% in the case of a 1.5 nm zone plate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of an additional lens with a large zone spacing in the middle of the stack can significantly improve the performance of the stack.
the use of a Fresnel zone plate with a larger outermost zone width is more effective than a smaller one in the context of a stacked Fresnel zone plate.
the use of two Fresnel zone plates is an efficient and practical approach for the fabrication of high-resolution X-ray lenses with a large field of view.
